subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with a narrower command set that already passes on Windows?
rationale: The coverage fits test-infrastructure priorities, but it changes recurring Windows runner scope and the active PR shows the broader command set is not yet safe in the target lane.

options.title: Fix build smoke before merge
options.body: Keep the requested command set but merge only after `pnpm build:strict-smoke` passes in native Windows PowerShell with redacted CI or terminal proof.

options.title: Narrow the first smoke
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage for already-proven contributor commands first and track build-smoke separately.

options.title: Pause CI expansion
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers settle Windows runner budget and smoke-command ownership.

recommendation.title: Fix build smoke before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the requested command set but merge only after `pnpm build:strict-smoke` passes in native Windows PowerShell with redacted CI or terminal proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow stabilization and the merged PowerShell-safe docs tooling repair.
